messages:
jamie_support: :rotating_light: Customer escalation: multiple hosted API requests returning 5xx/timeouts across a handful of tenants. Noticed spike ~10:12 UTC. Customer samples attached below. They report high latency followed by 502/504 and occasional 500s. Request ids: r-8f3a2, r-8f3a7, r-8f3b0. Hit rate for these customers jumped ~6x. Can SRE/infra triage?

ashley_sre: Adding context — I see a correlated increase in backend retries from the inference runtime starting 10:11:27 UTC and lots of KV cache errors. Stack indicates calls to prefix cache timed out and we then hit our gateway timeout. Putting logs here: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:11:30Z] runtime WARNING kv_cache.go:214 prefix-get failed: redis: read tcp 10.3.5.12:6379: i/o timeout
[2026-03-15T10:11:31Z] runtime ERROR request_handler.go:132 request r-8f3a2: fallback to cold path (no cache)
[2026-03-15T10:11:36Z] gateway ERROR gateway.go:87 request r-8f3a2: upstream 504 after 5s
```

noah_infra: I can confirm increased p95 latency on the redis cluster used by prefix caching (cache-prod-1). We have a few nodes reporting high iowait and evictions. Metrics: connection lat spikes, commands per sec up 4x. Looking at Cloud metrics now for disk and cpu.

matt_support: Customer_ops forwarded repro curl for the failing call. They included a minimal example that triggers 504 consistently. Putting details so engineers can reproduce locally against hosted endpoint: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"summarize: large prompt... (omitted)"}' \
 -v --stderr - | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Response: 504 Gateway Timeout after ~5s, no partial stream.

ashley_sre: Primary hypothesis: prefix/KV cache backend (Redis replica set) is overloaded/partially unavailable causing synchronous cache calls to block the request path. Runtime currently does a foreground prefix_lookup that waits up to 1.2s per shard; multiple shards ~= request blowup. When cache hangs, latency pushes past gateway timeout or triggers 500 when runtime errors bubble up.

sara_engineering: Can we move to an asynchronous cache fallback ASAP? If the runtime can treat cache timeouts as cache-miss and continue (but log), that should reduce 5xxs. I can patch a short-circuit to return miss after 150ms.

noah_infra: On infra side — I already moved two nodes out of rotation that had failed disk health checks. I'm seeing the cluster is in partial failover; replicas are lagging and a few clients are getting connection timeouts. Scaling up read capacity might help short-term. Spinning up two read-only Redis pods (bigger instance size) in the same AZ to relieve read pressure. ETA ~6-8 minutes.

ashley_sre: For immediate mitigation, let's flip the runtime KV call to soft-fail mode via runtime feature flag so requests won't block on redis. Feature flag: `runtime.kv.block_on_cache = false`. @noah_infra can you push this via the feature flag service? We'll roll it for hosted-prod only. This should both reduce 5xx and let traffic flow while infra heals.

noah_infra: Applying flag now to hosted-prod ring.

devops_bot: Flag update initiated: runtime.kv.block_on_cache -> false (hosted-prod) by noah_infra at 2026-03-15T10:18:12Z. Canary: 5%.

ashley_sre: Monitoring logs for changes...

sara_engineering: Quick patch is ready if we need to bump the canary to 100% and ship a revert later: commit 3f2b9ea. Patch makes prefix cache timeout 150ms and marks miss instead of throwing.

matt_support: Customers reporting fewer 5xxs in first wave post-flag: customer_ops sees success for r-8f3a2 retry. Keeping them updated.

noah_infra: New read nodes healthy and accepting connections. I see CMD Stats drop on overloaded nodes. Failover completed, cluster replicas resynced partially.

ashley_sre: Good. I'm seeing errors drop from ~18/min to ~2/min after flag. p95 latency for inference requests down from 1.2s to 480ms. Time window: 10:19–10:25 UTC. I'll keep monitoring for 30m before we revert flag.

jamie_support: Customer notes: The customer tried a few retries and backoff and saw improved behavior; they want a postmortem and whether this was customer-impacting SLA. They reported business impact (web hooks backlog). I've opened a ticket CC'ing customer success.

noah_infra: Root cause hypothesis: under-provisioned Redis read tier + sudden traffic pattern (large prefix reuse) caused connection saturation and node-level I/O pressure; triggers eviction + failover. Key points:
- small window of sustained high QPS from a few tenants (burst).
- redis eviction/IO resource exhausted -> timeouts.
- runtime's synchronous cache semantics amplify latency and push requests over gateway timeout.

ashley_sre: Remediation plan (short-term):
1) keep runtime.kv.block_on_cache = false for 30m to ensure stability.
2) increase read pool capacity on cache-prod-1 (done).
3) add blocking circuit-breaker in runtime when cache lat > 200ms to stop blocking new requests and fallback to miss.
4) postmortem and customer RCA.

sara_engineering: Longer term: adopt async prefix lookups + local LRU for very hot prefixes, and backpressure control on the runtime to avoid N*M blocking where N requests query M prefix shards. Also add per-customer burst protection to throttle heavy prefix scans.

devops_bot: Autoscaling event: new read-only pods created for cache-prod-1: redis-ro-12, redis-ro-13.

ashley_sre: I'm going to collect traces for the affected requests (r-8f3a2 etc). Please capture full KV timings and gateway spans. Also include the fallback path latencies.

matt_support: Logged a follow-up with customer (ticket #CS-2026-409). They asked for ETA on permanent fix and whether their data was impacted. I told them no data loss, only degraded service.

noah_infra: After load stabilized, we're seeing reduced CPU/iowait. Node health nominal. I'll keep the expanded read capacity for 48h while we validate.

jamie_support: Next actions:
- SRE & Infra to finalize short-term mitigations and confirm time to revert flag (ashley/noah).
- Eng to queue async-cache + circuit-breaker PR for prioritization (sara).
- Support to brief customers and prepare public incident note if this meets incident criteria (jamie/matt).

ashley_sre: I'll keep the flag at canary->100% now that infra is stable and errors are low. Rolling to 100% at 10:29 UTC.

devops_bot: Flag rollout complete: runtime.kv.block_on_cache -> false (hosted-prod) rolled to 100% at 2026-03-15T10:29:02Z.

sara_engineering: Opening tracking ticket ENG-2641 with proposed refactor: async prefix lookup, LRU hot-cache, fallback policy, per-customer rate limiter. ETA for initial PR: 2 weeks.

jamie_support: Will draft incident summary and share with customer success. If anything regresses, ping this thread and we'll reopen escalation. Thanks all for fast responses. :thumbsup:

customer_ops: Customer confirmation: they saw recovery after 10:20 UTC. Appreciative of the quick patch. Asked for timeline for preventing recurrence.

ashley_sre: Noted. We'll include timeline in the postmortem. Closing monitoring loop but leaving ENG/INF tickets open.

jamie_support: Closing thread for now — will attach postmortem link once available.
